blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A “very strong El Nino” event has formed in the tropical Pacific and is expected to peak by the end of the year, a state weather bureau official said on Wednesday, with lingering impacts likely to persist through mid-2027. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) is expected to issue its sixth El Nino advisory later today that warns the climate phenomenon has intensified into a “very strong” event that threatens to worsen drought conditions, according to the weather bureau’s climate monitoring chief Ana Liza Solis. “As of today, a very strong El Nino is now […]...
